target.title: fix(macos): preserve device identity storage
target.body:
## Summary
The macOS identity store no longer chooses App Group storage unless the running bundle has the matching `com.apple.security.application-groups` entitlement. Unentitled macOS app builds fall back to the legacy Application Support identity directory instead of repeatedly using an App Group path they cannot reliably persist.

Existing unrecognized `identity/device.json` files are also preserved in both the Swift and TypeScript loaders. The loader can still return a fresh in-memory identity when it cannot decode the file, but it no longer replaces existing identity bytes unless it is creating a missing file or performing a proven safe normalization.

## Root cause
`apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/DeviceIdentity.swift` selected App Group storage whenever `FileManager.containerURL(forSecurityApplicationGroupIdentifier:)` returned a URL:

```before
if let appGroupStateDirURL {
    return appGroupStateDirURL
}
```

On affected shipped macOS builds, that could select the App Group container even though the bundle did not carry the matching App Groups entitlement. When persistence at that path failed, `loadOrCreate` returned generated identities, leading to pairing churn.

The Swift and TypeScript `loadOrCreate` implementations also treated an existing but unrecognized identity file like a missing file:

```before
case .unknown:
    break
```

That path generated and saved a new identity over existing bytes.

## Fix
Swift now checks the running bundle entitlement before selecting App Group identity storage:

```after
if appGroupStateDirAvailable, let appGroupStateDirURL {
    return appGroupStateDirURL
}
```

When the entitlement is absent, the existing legacy Application Support fallback wins. Both loaders now preserve existing unrecognized identity files and only persist a generated identity when the file is missing:

```after
if FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: url.path) {
    return self.generate()
}
```

## Why this is the right boundary
The storage decision belongs in `DeviceIdentityPaths`, because every Swift caller reaches identity storage through that path resolver. The no-overwrite guard belongs in the identity loaders, because Swift and TypeScript both own `identity/device.json` and must preserve existing state consistently.

This does not add a new migration or compatibility branch. It narrows steady-state storage selection to a bundle capability the app actually has, and it keeps existing identity bytes intact when the loader cannot prove a safe normalization.

## Verification
- `PATH=/opt/node/bin:$PATH PNPM_CONFIG_MODULES_DIR=/root/openclaw/node_modules node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/device-identity.test.ts` passed.
- `PATH=/opt/node/bin:$PATH /root/openclaw/node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/DeviceIdentity.swift apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Tests/OpenClawKitTests/DeviceIdentityStoreTests.swift src/infra/device-identity.ts src/infra/device-identity.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- New TypeScript regression fails on pristine main and passes with this patch.
- `swift --version` failed locally with `swift: command not found`, so `cd apps/shared/OpenClawKit && swift test --filter DeviceIdentityStoreTests` was not run in this container.
- `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --help` failed its Crabbox binary sanity check, `/root/crabbox/bin/crabbox` is missing, and `go version` is not installed, so remote Swift/macOS validation was unavailable here.
- `PATH=/opt/node/bin:$PATH node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/infra/device-identity.ts src/infra/device-identity.test.ts` was blocked before target linting by an unrelated Telegram boundary artifact error in `extensions/telegram/src/bot-info.ts`.
- `PATH=/opt/node/bin:$PATH node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo` was blocked by unrelated missing UI package resolution for `@openclaw/uirouter`, `@openclaw/libterminal/browser`, and `ghostty-web` in this fresh worktree dependency layout.
- Autoreview closeout could not initialize because the in-process app-server client hit a read-only filesystem error.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: Existing identity storage was selected or rewritten in ways that could make the same macOS installation present a new device identity.
Real environment tested: Node 22.19 on Linux drove the production TypeScript identity loader against a real on-disk `identity/device.json` on pristine main `6bc661ce14c83ab854118a166197e318eea9ee87` and on this patched tree; the Swift App Group entitlement branch was not executed in a signed macOS app here.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: Imported `src/infra/device-identity.ts` with `node --import tsx`, wrote the same existing unrecognized `identity/device.json`, invoked `loadOrCreateDeviceIdentity(file)`, and read the file back from disk.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 6bc661ce14)
identityMatchesStoredExample=no
fileChanged=yes
storedKeys=createdAtMs,deviceId,privateKeyPem,publicKeyPem,version
stableDeviceIdStillPresent=no
# AFTER (this patch, identical input)
identityMatchesStoredExample=no
fileChanged=no
storedKeys=schema,stableDeviceId
stableDeviceIdStillPresent=yes
```
Observed result after fix: The same existing identity file changes on main and remains byte-for-byte unchanged after this patch, so the loader no longer replaces preserved identity state with a generated stored record.
What was not tested: No signed macOS app restart on macOS 27 was run here; local Swift and remote Crabbox validation were unavailable in this container.

## Related
Fixes #99283.
Related to #99522.
Distinct from #79715, which fixed Swift and TypeScript schema compatibility but did not make App Group selection entitlement-aware.
